decisions.question: How are the ten slices of D2 ordered under fp-progression: every slice's pure part in one pure band before any effect phase, or each pure part just before its own slice's effects, with virtual time as phase 2 as the node's Development flow words it?

options.label: Strict bands
options.consequence: Pure band nidana.runtime.2 to .4 as three parallel lanes right after the surface; virtual time becomes phase 5. Matches the conventions line 'pure-core phases precede every effect phase'; the pure phases run no behavior replay, so 'no behavior replay before virtual time' still holds.

options.label: Pure part before its own effects
options.consequence: Virtual time is phase 2 as the Development flow's literal order reads; module counts, telemetry mapping and recorder queries land late, interleaved with effect phases, against the conventions' band rule.

decisions.why: The conventions' fp-progression line is the governing text and says pure-core phases precede every effect phase. The node's Development flow constraint behind 'virtual time comes next' is about behavior replays, and the pure band runs none. Signal that would change it: the owner reading 'Virtual time comes next' as a phase number rather than as the first effect.

decisions.question: Where do start() and shutdown() land, given that the Slices table puts the startup barrier and shutdown in the lifecycle slice, which closes the plan?

options.label: start with the publish path, shutdown incremental (D8)
options.consequence: start() and the startup queue land with the publish path; shutdown() lands as the lifecycle transition with bus construction and each effect phase adds its slice's teardown and its rejection after shutdown; the last phase keeps the startup window, onShutdown and G36's order. Delivery guarantees replay from the ownership phase on.

options.label: Lifecycle whole in the last phase
options.consequence: One diff for shutdown, but 66 of 95 bus-api@v1 cases and 23 of 45 bus-testing@v1 cases call start(), and bus-api@v1 G8, G18 and bus-testing@v1 G5, G9, G14, G17, G18 call shutdown(), so almost no behavior replays before the last phase.

decisions.chosen: start with the publish path, shutdown incremental (D8)
decisions.why: The suites cannot replay delivery without start(), and several non-lifecycle guarantees assert on shutdown; incremental teardown keeps each slice's shutdown with the code that owns the resource. Recorded as D8. Signal that would change it: a reviewer who wants all of shutdown in one diff.

decisions.question: How do gates check bus-api@v1 G38, G39 and bus-testing@v1 G20 ('checked by nidana.runtime's gates'), given that every gate must be an fvm command?

options.label: Package test plus one provider library (D9)
options.consequence: A test in packages/nidana_dart_runtime/test checks the pubspec and the sources; every timer and microtask goes through one internal provider library, so the check can forbid Timer( and the global scheduleMicrotask( elsewhere; the pipeline gets its timer through its port.

options.label: grep in each gate
options.consequence: Not an fvm command, not run with the package's tests.

options.label: Review only
options.consequence: zone.run at each call site cannot be told apart from a timer outside the zone by a source check.

decisions.chosen: Package test plus one provider library (D9)
decisions.why: ADR-003 Consequences anticipates a source search for DateTime.now(, Stopwatch( and timers outside the provider implementation; a Dart test keeps the gate an fvm command, and model-gate-commands showed fvm dart test packages/{member} runs from the workspace root. Recorded as D9.

decisions.question: Is the delivery slice one phase or several?

options.label: Pure core, registry and cells, publish path; ownership separate
options.consequence: Four phases of about 330 to 420 lines each (nidana.runtime.2, .6, .7, .8); .6 replays no guarantee of its own because its cases publish through publishers.

options.label: One delivery phase plus ownership
options.consequence: About 850 lines, two PEs in one review sitting.

decisions.chosen: Pure core, registry and cells, publish path; ownership separate
decisions.why: The stand-in's registry, cells, publish path, observers and recorder seam are about 400 lines without docs or tests (docs/auto-run/experiments/bus-api-widened/packages/nidana_dart_runtime/lib/src/bus.dart); the PE ceiling forces the split.

decisions.question: Is the pipeline one phase or two?

options.label: Two phases
options.consequence: Synchronous stages and sinks first (.9), then switchMap, retry, time stages and cancellation (.10), which need the virtual scheduler.

options.label: One phase
options.consequence: About 750 lines with tests; one review sitting cannot hold it.

decisions.why: The stand-in interpreter alone is 438 lines; the split follows ADR-003 items 3 and 4, which govern the second half only.

decisions.question: Is activation one phase or two?

options.label: Checks and handles, then wiring
options.consequence: nidana.runtime.11 (planOf, idempotency, limits, analyses, handles, ownership, live graph, activation observers) runs beside the pipeline lane; nidana.runtime.12 implements the port and the connection timing and binds the live suite. Each replays guarantees of its own.

options.label: One activation phase
options.consequence: About 660 lines and 8 or more tasks, above the PE; the connection timing reviewed together with the checks.

decisions.why: Merged it exceeds the PE; the read path's timing (D3) is the seam that moved most in the experiments (D1 point 4), which is a stated reason to review it in isolation. The fixtures confirm the split has replay value: G1, G10, G20, G21, G24, G32, G37 pass without wiring.

decisions.question: Where do the small slices go: telemetry (about 100 lines) and the residual lifecycle (startup window, onShutdown, G36 order)?

options.label: Telemetry with test support, lifecycle with module scopes
options.consequence: Two phases of about 330 and 400 lines; each pair is a sizing-floor merge (same tier, no third phase needs one without the other).

options.label: Separate phases
options.consequence: Two phases below the floor whose process artifacts would exceed their diffs.

decisions.chosen: Telemetry with test support, lifecycle with module scopes
decisions.why: The sizing floor: a phase must earn its cycle; telemetry alone and the residual lifecycle alone do not. Signal that would change it: a separate owner for observability.

decisions.question: When does a guarantee join a producing gate's --guarantee list?

options.label: When every case of it can pass
options.consequence: Lists derived case by case from the fixtures; several guarantees replay later than the phase that implements their slice (delivery guarantees from the ownership phase on).

options.label: When its slice lands
options.consequence: Gates would fail: most cases publish through publishers, call start(), or activate a topology.

decisions.chosen: When every case of it can pass
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 10 restricts behavior to the guarantees delivered so far, and a gate must pass; a case runs only when every id it covers is in the restriction (item 9). The derivation is mechanical and reproducible.

decisions.question: How are producing phases' gates written: 'node default plus' the replay, or the full command?

options.label: Full command per producing phase
options.consequence: Each producing phase's Gate is a complete fvm chain; hsdd-config copies it verbatim into the phase context and the superpowers derivative.

options.label: node default plus replay
options.consequence: Shorter, but hsdd-config replaces only a Gate that is exactly 'node default', so the context could carry an unresolved phrase.

decisions.why: hsdd-config's switch rule resolves 'node default' only as the whole Gate value; the full command avoids an implementing session guessing the default.
evidence: .agents/skills/hsdd-config/SKILL.md (The Generic Phase Context, The Superpowers Derivative)

decisions.question: How are the pipeline phases verified before activation composes them?

options.label: Unit tests against a port of the test's own
options.consequence: As D2 and the Isolation strategy state; the live suite replays through Bus.activate from the wiring phase on.

options.label: Bind the live suite to a test-local mini bus
options.consequence: Earlier coverage of topology-dsl@v1 G18 to G29, but the harness would re-implement delivery, dedup and reentrancy in test code, about 150 to 200 lines more per phase.

decisions.chosen: Unit tests against a port of the test's own
decisions.why: D2 already decided it; a test-local bus that passes the live suite is a second runtime to maintain. Signal that would change it: a pipeline defect that the unit tests missed and the live suite caught at the wiring phase.

decisions.question: Does the pipeline reuse the delivery core's per-read dedup state, making nidana.runtime.9 depend on nidana.runtime.2?

options.label: Reuse the delivery core's dedup
options.consequence: One implementation for observed subscriptions and topology reads (bus-api@v1 G16, topology-dsl@v1 G19); .9 waits on .2.

options.label: Pipeline's own dedup
options.consequence: .9 depends only on the package; two implementations of one rule.

decisions.why: G16 and live G19 state the same rule; one function keeps them from drifting, and .2 is an early pure phase, so the wait is short.

decisions.question: Does test support and telemetry (nidana.runtime.13) wait on activation wiring, or run beside it after ownership with a smaller replay?

options.label: Wait on activation wiring
options.consequence: Its gate replays bus-testing@v1 G3, G12 to G19 and bus-api@v1 G33, whose cases activate topologies; serial anyway, since both edit lib/src/bus.dart.

options.label: Run beside activation
options.consequence: Its gate could replay only bus-testing@v1 G15 and G16; the rest would join at a later gate, and the two phases would still serialize on bus.dart.

decisions.why: The collision on bus.dart (TestBus) serializes them regardless; waiting lets the phase replay what it delivers.

decisions.question: Which phases are listed as producing bus-api@v1 and bus-testing@v1?

options.label: Phases that implement public members
options.consequence: bus-api@v1 [.1, .5, .6, .7, .8, .11, .12, .13, .14], bus-testing@v1 [.1, .5, .7, .13, .14]; .6 and .7 produce members whose guarantees replay later; pure and pipeline phases produce none.

options.label: Phases that add a replayed guarantee
options.consequence: Drops .6 and bus-testing's .7, hiding where observe, getCurrentValue and the recorder seam are implemented.

decisions.why: Reconcile writes the Delivery paragraph from the confirms and the gates' lists; naming the implementing phases and saying when their guarantees replay tells consumers both facts.

decisions.question: Phase 1 is above the ~400-line PE (about 420 lines). Split it?

options.label: Keep one phase
options.consequence: Gate-only, mostly declarations and doc comments; the replay checks it mechanically.

options.label: Split
options.consequence: ADR-001 item 10 runs surface and reject in full from the first producing phase, so each contract's declarations must land in one phase, and the two contracts share a library (D1 point 1).

decisions.why: The split is not allowed by ADR-001 item 10; the overage is small and declaration-heavy.

decisions.question: Review tiers for the effect phases: full-review throughout, or spot-check for the ownership phase?

options.label: full-review for every effect phase but test support
options.consequence: Ownership (single-writer enforcement), delivery timing, activation and the scheduler are business logic and orchestration; test support and telemetry are well constrained by their suites.

options.label: spot-check for ownership
options.consequence: Lighter review of the claims check, which enforces Spec §3.11 layer 1.

decisions.chosen: full-review for every effect phase but test support
decisions.why: The skill puts orchestration and business logic at full-review; single-writer enforcement is a guarantee consumers rely on for correctness.

decisions.question: amend bus-api@v1 G41's outside clause per D5: can it break a consumer?

options.label: Compatible
options.consequence: The clause stated no behavior for an off-type value; nothing changes for a value of the topic's value type.

options.label: Breaking
options.consequence: Reconcile takes it to the human.

decisions.why: It adds behavior where the contract was silent, and no fixture of any contract publishes an off-type value; evidence in docs/auto-run/experiments/off-type-delivery/.

decisions.question: amend bus-testing@v1 G16 per D6: can it break a consumer?

options.label: Compatible
options.consequence: Identity holds wherever G16 could hold it; only a widened envelope gets an equal copy where the old wording threw.

options.label: Breaking
options.consequence: Reconcile takes it to the human.

decisions.why: Probe P2 showed the earlier wording threw a TypeError for exactly the case that changes; == comparisons hold in both cases.

decisions.question: amend bus-testing@v1 G18 per D7: can it break a consumer?

options.label: Compatible
options.consequence: Only calls for one topic at two type arguments change, where the old wording could not hold; one publisher per topic keeps one claim.

options.label: Breaking
options.consequence: Reconcile takes it to the human.

decisions.why: T7 in bus-api-widened showed the old wording fails at run time for that case.

experiments.question: For each conformance case of bus-api@v1, bus-testing@v1 and topology-dsl@v1's live suite, after which phase of this plan can it pass, and so at which phase does each guarantee join the cumulative --guarantee list? How many cases call start() and shutdown()?
experiments.finding: bus-api@v1: G3 at .5; G4, G11 at .7; G7, G8, G12, G13, G15, G17 to G19, G29 to G31 at .8; G1, G10, G20, G21, G24, G32, G37 at .11; G6, G9, G14, G16, G22, G23, G25, G26, G34, G41 at .12; G33 at .13; G5, G27, G28, G35, G36 at .14. bus-testing@v1: G5 to G8, G10, G11 at .5; G3, G12 to G19 at .13; G4, G9 at .14. Live suite G18 to G29 at .12. 66 of 95 bus-api cases and 23 of 45 bus-testing cases call start(); shutdown() appears in bus-api G8, G18, G36 and bus-testing G5, G9, G14, G17, G18. The classification is a regex over case bodies plus a hand list of activation cases that need no pipeline wiring; it is a planning estimate that the first real gates confirm.
